backrank_1.title: Back-Rank Mate 1
backrank_1.instruction: Black to move. Deliver checkmate on the back rank.
backrank_1.concept: When a king is hemmed in on the back rank by its own pawns, a rook or queen check along that rank is checkmate — the king has no escape square.
backrank_1.takeaway: Before attacking, check: can the enemy king leave the back rank?
narration: Move 1: Qe1+ — forcing check. the back-rank mate keeps the initiative: every reply is bad.
Move 2: Rxe1+ — check with capture! the back-rank mate wins material with tempo.
Move 3: Rxe1# — the back-rank mate delivers checkmate. Before attacking, check: can the enemy king leave the back rank?
hints: The enemy king is trapped by its own pawns. Check along the back rank.
The key move starts with Qe1+.
backrank_1.mistakeText: That does not mate — look for the check the king cannot escape. Its own pawns block every flight square.
backrank_1.explanation: Before attacking, check: can the enemy king leave the back rank? Solutions: Qe1+, Rxe1+, Rxe1#.

quiz.question: Why is a back-rank check usually decisive?
options: The king has no escape squares — its own pawns block it
Rooks are worth more than pawns

mate1_1.title: Mate in 1 1
mate1_1.instruction: White to move. Find the move that checkmates immediately.
mate1_1.concept: Mate in one means a single move ends the game. Scan every check first, then ask: after this check, does the king have any legal move or block?
mate1_1.takeaway: Checks first, captures second, quiet moves last.
narration: Move 1: Re7# — the mate in one delivers checkmate. Checks first, captures second, quiet moves last.
hints: There is exactly one mating move. Start by listing all checks.
The key move starts with Re7#.
mate1_1.mistakeText: That is not mate — the king escapes or the check is blocked. List every check and test each one.
mate1_1.explanation: Checks first, captures second, quiet moves last. Solution: Re7#.

quiz.question: What should you examine first when hunting mate in 1?
options: Every checking move, testing each escape

mate2_1.title: Mate in 2 1
mate2_1.instruction: Black to move. Force checkmate in two moves.
mate2_1.concept: A forced mate in two works against every defence. Your first move limits the king, and the second finishes — no matter which legal reply comes.
mate2_1.takeaway: First move takes away flight squares; second move delivers.
narration: Move 1: Qh2+ — forcing check. the forced mate keeps the initiative: every reply is bad.
Move 2: Qh1# — the forced mate delivers checkmate. First move takes away flight squares; second move delivers.
hints: Take away the king’s flight squares first — the mate follows itself.
The key move starts with Qh2+.
mate2_1.mistakeText: That allows an escape. Your first move must work against every legal reply, not just one.
mate2_1.explanation: First move takes away flight squares; second move delivers. Solutions: Qh2+, Qh1#.

quiz.question: What makes a combination "forced"?

fork_1.explanation: Attack two things at once; you win one of them. Solutions: Nc5+, Nxa6.

pin_1.title: The Pin 1
pin_1.instruction: Black to move. Exploit the pin to win material.
pin_1.concept: A piece is pinned when moving it would expose something more valuable — the king (absolute pin) or a queen or rook (relative pin). Pinned pieces are prisoners: attack them, or attack what they can no longer defend.
pin_1.takeaway: Pin first, win the piece second.
narration: Move 1: Rxc1+ — check with capture! the pin wins material with tempo.
Move 2: Bc5 — the pin. Pin first, win the piece second.
hints: Find the piece that cannot move — then take what it used to defend.
The key move starts with Rxc1+.
pin_1.mistakeText: That ignores the pin. Ask: which enemy piece cannot move, and what did it stop defending?
pin_1.explanation: Pin first, win the piece second. Solutions: Rxc1+, Bc5.

quiz.question: What is an absolute pin?
options: A pin where moving would expose the king — the piece cannot legally move

skewer_1.title: The Skewer 1
skewer_1.instruction: White to move. Skewer and win the piece behind.
skewer_1.concept: A skewer is the reverse of a pin: you attack the valuable piece first, and when it moves, you capture the piece hiding behind it. Line pieces — rooks, bishops, queens — skewer.
skewer_1.takeaway: Hit the big piece; collect the piece behind it.
narration: Move 1: Rh8+ — forcing check. the skewer keeps the initiative: every reply is bad.
Move 2: Rxa8 — the skewer collects material. Hit the big piece; collect the piece behind it.
hints: Two enemy pieces stand on one line. Hit the valuable one first.
The key move starts with Rh8+.
skewer_1.mistakeText: That is not the skewer — attack the more valuable piece first so it must move and expose the piece behind.
skewer_1.explanation: Hit the big piece; collect the piece behind it. Solutions: Rh8+, Rxa8.

quiz.question: How is a skewer different from a pin?
options: You attack the valuable piece first and win what hides behind it

discovered_1.title: Discovered Attacks 1
discovered_1.instruction: White to move. Unleash the discovered attack.
discovered_1.concept: Move a piece out of the way and the piece behind it suddenly attacks. The moving piece can itself give check or grab something — two threats from one move.
discovered_1.takeaway: One move, two threats: the mover and the unveiled.
narration: Move 1: Qxe7+ — check with capture! the discovered attack wins material with tempo.
Move 2: Bxc4 — the discovered attack collects material. One move, two threats: the mover and the unveiled.
hints: One of your pieces is masked. Move the blocker with tempo.
The key move starts with Qxe7+.
discovered_1.mistakeText: That unleashes nothing. Find the piece whose path is blocked — move the blocker with a threat.
discovered_1.explanation: One move, two threats: the mover and the unveiled. Solutions: Qxe7+, Bxc4.

quiz.question: Why are discovered attacks so dangerous?
options: They create two threats at once — the moving piece and the unveiled piece

attraction_1.title: Attraction 1

interference_1.title: Interference 1
interference_1.instruction: Black to move. Interfere with the defender’s line.
interference_1.concept: Defenders work along lines. Throw a piece onto that line — even as a sacrifice — and the defence is cut. The defender watches helplessly from the wrong side of your piece.
interference_1.takeaway: Cut the line, kill the defence.
narration: Move 1: Rxh4+ — check with capture! the interference wins material with tempo.
Move 2: Rxg5+ — check with capture! the interference wins material with tempo.
hints: The defender guards along a line. Drop a piece onto that line.
The key move starts with Rxh4+.
interference_1.mistakeText: That leaves the defensive line intact. Interpose on the line between defender and its charge.
interference_1.explanation: Cut the line, kill the defence. Solutions: Rxh4+, Rxg5+.

xray_1.title: X-Ray Attack 1
xray_1.instruction: Black to move. Strike through with the x-ray.
xray_1.concept: An x-ray attack hits through an enemy piece to the target behind — typically rook versus king on the same file, where the piece in between cannot survive the pressure.
xray_1.takeaway: Line up on the real target, whatever stands between.
narration: Move 1: Rxb1+ — check with capture! the x-ray wins material with tempo.
Move 2: Rxb1# — the x-ray delivers checkmate. Line up on the real target, whatever stands between.
hints: Your rook sees through to the king — the piece between is doomed.
The key move starts with Rxb1+.
xray_1.mistakeText: That ignores the piece behind. Line up through the blocker onto the true target.
xray_1.explanation: Line up on the real target, whatever stands between. Solutions: Rxb1+, Rxb1#.

quiz.question: An x-ray attack means…
options: Attacking a target through a piece standing between

zugzwang_1.title: Zugzwang 1
zugzwang_1.instruction: Black to move. Put the opponent in zugzwang.
zugzwang_1.concept: Zugzwang: any move the opponent makes worsens their position. Common in pawn endgames — triangulate, lose a tempo, and force them to abandon a key square.
zugzwang_1.takeaway: When everything wins, pass the move to them.
narration: Move 1: Kf5 — the zugzwang. When everything wins, pass the move to them.
Move 2: Kg4 — the zugzwang. When everything wins, pass the move to them.
hints: Do not rush — make a waiting move that keeps every threat alive.
The key move starts with Kf5.
zugzwang_1.mistakeText: That releases the tension too early. Improve your position first, then force them to move.
zugzwang_1.explanation: When everything wins, pass the move to them. Solutions: Kf5, Kg4.

quiz.question: What is zugzwang?
options: A position where any move the opponent makes loses

intermezzo_1.title: Intermezzo 1
intermezzo_1.instruction: White to move. Find the intermezzo.
intermezzo_1.concept: Instead of the "obvious" recapture, slip in an intermediate threat first — a check or an attack — and recapture afterwards under better circumstances.
intermezzo_1.takeaway: Obvious recaptures can wait. Threaten first.
narration: Move 1: Bxc6+ — check with capture! the in-between move wins material with tempo.
Move 2: Qxc3 — the in-between move collects material. Obvious recaptures can wait. Threaten first.
hints: Before recapturing, is there a check or threat to insert?
The key move starts with Bxc6+.
intermezzo_1.mistakeText: That is the automatic recapture — look for the forcing move you can insert first.
intermezzo_1.explanation: Obvious recaptures can wait. Threaten first. Solutions: Bxc6+, Qxc3.

quiz.question: An intermezzo is…
options: An unexpected forcing move played before the "obvious" reply

capdef_1.title: Removing the Defender 1
capdef_1.instruction: Black to move. Remove the defender.
capdef_1.concept: If one piece guards everything, capture it — even at apparent cost. Once the guard is gone, the treasure behind it falls.
capdef_1.takeaway: One guard, one capture, then collect.
narration: Move 1: Bxf3 — removing the defender collects material. One guard, one capture, then collect.
Move 2: Bxd4 — removing the defender collects material. One guard, one capture, then collect.
hints: A single piece guards the target. Eliminate that guard.
The key move starts with Bxf3.
capdef_1.mistakeText: That leaves the guard in place. Capture the defender first, whatever it costs.
capdef_1.explanation: One guard, one capture, then collect. Solutions: Bxf3, Bxd4.

quiz.question: When is capturing the defender correct?
options: When the piece it guards is worth more than the cost of the capture

sacrifice_1.title: The Sacrifice 1
sacrifice_1.instruction: White to move. Sacrifice for the attack.
sacrifice_1.concept: Give up material for something greater: an exposed king, a crushing initiative, or a forced mate. A sound sacrifice is calculated to the end; a positional one trusts lasting pressure.
sacrifice_1.takeaway: Count the compensation, not the material.
narration: Move 1: Qxh7+ — check with capture! the sacrifice wins material with tempo.
Move 2: Rh4# — the sacrifice delivers checkmate. Count the compensation, not the material.
hints: Material matters less than the king. Break through, whatever it costs.
The key move starts with Qxh7+.
sacrifice_1.mistakeText: That gives material for nothing. A sacrifice needs concrete compensation — mate, king hunt, or lasting pressure.
sacrifice_1.explanation: Count the compensation, not the material. Solutions: Qxh7+, Rh4#.

quiz.question: What makes a sacrifice sound?
options: Concrete compensation: mate, an exposed king, or lasting pressure

queenend_1.title: Queen Endgames 1
queenend_1.instruction: Black to move. Navigate the queen endgame.
queenend_1.concept: Queen endgames swing between promotion races and perpetual checks. Centralize the queen, escort your pawn from the side, and never let the enemy queen settle into endless checks.
queenend_1.takeaway: Central queen, sideways escort, no perpetuals.
narration: Move 1: Qxd5+ — check with capture! queen centralization wins material with tempo.
Move 2: a3 — queen centralization. Central queen, sideways escort, no perpetuals.
Move 3: a2 — queen centralization. Central queen, sideways escort, no perpetuals.
hints: Centralize the queen and time the pawn advance.
The key move starts with Qxd5+.
queenend_1.mistakeText: That allows endless checks or loses the race. Centralize and time the pawn push.
queenend_1.explanation: Central queen, sideways escort, no perpetuals. Solutions: Qxd5+, a3, a2.

bishopend_1.title: Bishop Endgames 1
bishopend_1.instruction: White to move. Handle the bishop endgame.
bishopend_1.concept: Same-color bishop endings are drawish; opposite-color ones favor the attacker. Fix enemy pawns on your bishop’s color and use your king as the battering ram.
bishopend_1.takeaway: Fix pawns on your color; march the king.
narration: Move 1: b6 — the color complex. Fix pawns on your color; march the king.
Move 2: b7 — the color complex. Fix pawns on your color; march the king.
hints: Pawns fixed on your bishop’s color are targets. Attack them with king and bishop.
The key move starts with b6.
bishopend_1.mistakeText: That ignores the color battle. Fix their pawns on your bishop’s color first.
bishopend_1.explanation: Fix pawns on your color; march the king. Solutions: b6, b7.

quiz.question: Why do opposite-color bishop endings favor the attacker?
options: The defender’s bishop can never guard what the attacker’s bishop attacks

knightend_1.title: Knight Endgames 1
knightend_1.instruction: Black to move. Outplay the knight endgame.
knightend_1.concept: Knights need outposts and short distances. Dominate the enemy knight by attacking everything it defends, and push pawns on the side your knight controls.
knightend_1.takeaway: Outpost first, then push where the knight points.
narration: Move 1: h3 — the outpost. Outpost first, then push where the knight points.
Move 2: h2 — the outpost. Outpost first, then push where the knight points.
Move 3: h1=Q — the outpost. Outpost first, then push where the knight points.
hints: Find the outpost square your knight can never be chased from.
The key move starts with h3.
knightend_1.mistakeText: That drifts without a plan. Plant the knight on its best square, then advance there.
knightend_1.explanation: Outpost first, then push where the knight points. Solutions: h3, h2, h1=Q.

quiz.question: What is a knight outpost?
options: A square on the enemy’s side that cannot be attacked by a pawn

narration: Move 1: h2 — the outpost. Outpost first, then push where the knight points.
Move 2: c3 — the outpost. Outpost first, then push where the knight points.
hints: Find the outpost square your knight can never be chased from.
The key move starts with h2.
knightend_6.mistakeText: That drifts without a plan. Plant the knight on its best square, then advance there.
knightend_6.explanation: Outpost first, then push where the knight points. Solutions: h2, c3.

quiz.question: What is a knight outpost?
options: A square on the enemy’s side that cannot be attacked by a pawn

qrend_1.title: Queen vs Rook Endings 1

qrend_1.explanation: No fortresses: keep tension until the rook cracks. Solution: Rh4#.

promotion_1.title: Promotion Tactics 1
promotion_1.instruction: White to move. Force the promotion through.
promotion_1.concept: Pushing a passed pawn through takes calculation: count the race, sacrifice to clear the path, and remember underpromotion when stalemate or a knight fork threatens.
promotion_1.takeaway: Count the squares, clear the path, queen with check when you can.
narration: Move 1: h7 — the promotion. Count the squares, clear the path, queen with check when you can.
Move 2: h8=Q — the promotion. Count the squares, clear the path, queen with check when you can.
hints: Count the race first — then clear the pawn’s path by force.
The key move starts with h7.
promotion_1.mistakeText: That mis-times the race. Count moves to queen for both sides before pushing.
promotion_1.explanation: Count the squares, clear the path, queen with check when you can. Solutions: h7, h8=Q.

quiz.question: When is underpromotion correct?
options: To avoid stalemate or to deliver a knight fork/check

advpawn_1.title: Advanced Pawns 1
advpawn_1.instruction: White to move. Push the passer through.
advpawn_1.concept: A far-advanced pawn ties down whole armies. Support it with the king, use breakthrough sacrifices to open lines, and never push without counting the reply.
narration: Move 1: b6 — the passed pawn. Supported passers win games.
Move 2: b7 — the passed pawn. Supported passers win games.
hints: Support the passer with the king before pushing it further.
The key move starts with b6.
advpawn_1.mistakeText: That pushes without support. Bring the king up first — lone passers get rounded up.
advpawn_1.explanation: Supported passers win games. Solutions: b6, b7.

quiz.question: What makes a passed pawn strong?
options: No enemy pawn can stop it, especially with king support

kingside_1.title: Kingside Attacks 1
kingside_1.instruction: White to move. Break through on the kingside.
kingside_1.concept: Attack the king where it lives: open lines toward it, bring every piece, and strike before the defender consolidates. Pawn storms, piece sacrifices to open the h-file, and mating nets all belong here.
kingside_1.takeaway: Speed kills: attack with everything before they defend.
narration: Move 1: Qxh7# — the breakthrough delivers checkmate. Speed kills: attack with everything before they defend.
hints: Open a line to the king and pile every piece onto it.
The key move starts with Qxh7#.
kingside_1.mistakeText: That is too slow — the defence will consolidate. Every move must threaten or bring a new attacker.
kingside_1.explanation: Speed kills: attack with everything before they defend. Solution: Qxh7#.

quiz.question: The golden rule of a kingside attack is…
options: Attack fast with everything — do not let them consolidate

exposed_1.title: Exposed Kings 1
exposed_1.instruction: White to move. Punish the exposed king.
exposed_1.concept: A king caught in the center or stripped of pawn cover is a target for the rest of the game. Open the position, keep queens on, and hunt it — do not let it castle by hand.
exposed_1.takeaway: Open lines against an uncastled king, always.
narration: Move 1: Rf8+ — forcing check. the king hunt keeps the initiative: every reply is bad.
Move 2: R1f7+ — forcing check. the king hunt keeps the initiative: every reply is bad.
Move 3: Rh8# — the king hunt delivers checkmate. Open lines against an uncastled king, always.
hints: The king has no shelter — open lines and bring checks.
The key move starts with Rf8+.
exposed_1.mistakeText: That lets the king escape to safety. Keep the position open and the pressure on.
exposed_1.explanation: Open lines against an uncastled king, always. Solutions: Rf8+, R1f7+, Rh8#.

quiz.question: Against an uncastled king you should…

narration: Move 1: Nxf4 — the conversion collects material. Better means: improve, restrict, then collect.
